canonical.title: Eat Penang: A Street-Food Pilgrim's Field Guide to George Town & Beyond

siblings.title: Sleep — Penang: Heritage Shophouses, Colonial Grandes Dames & Hill Retreats
siblings.summary: Where a couple should sleep in George Town and beyond — restored shophouses, the Blue Mansion, the E&O, design conversions, beach character and a hill retreat.

siblings.title: Do — Penang: semi-adventurous activities & day-trips from George Town
siblings.summary: Penang Hill + The Habitat canopy walks, national-park treks, Balik Pulau cycling, kayaking, snorkelling and the street-art trail, rated for difficulty, time and cost.

siblings.title: See Penang: The Unmissable Icons of George Town & Beyond
siblings.summary: First-timer's guide to Penang's must-see icons: the UNESCO core, street art, clan houses, jetties, temples and Penang Hill, with 2026 hours and prices.

siblings.title: Offbeat Penang: Vipers, Ghost Tunnels, Pig-Blood Noodles and a Mosque on Stilts
siblings.summary: Twenty-odd weird, eerie and unexpected Penang finds a first-timer walks straight past.

siblings.title: Culture in Penang: A First-Timer's Guide to Museums, Festivals & Crafts
siblings.summary: When to come for Penang's festivals, which museums are worth it, and the heritage crafts you can try yourself.

siblings.title: Around & Day-Trips: Getting In, Out and About Penang
siblings.summary: How a couple based in George Town arrives, leaves and explores Penang — hops from KL/Cameron Highlands, onward to Langkawi, local transport and the day-trip orbit.

sources.title: https://www.timetravelturtle.com/malaysia/best-food-in-penang/
sources.claim: 2026 George Town dish-by-dish guide with named stalls, locations and RM prices (CKT RM6, assam laksa Joo Hooi RM5, cendol RM2.90, pasembur Hussain).

sources.title: https://www.willflyforfood.net/penang-food-guide-15-must-eat-restaurants-street-food-stalls-in-penang-malaysia/
sources.claim: Named must-eat stalls with addresses and opening days: Kheng Pin (lor bak, closed Mon), Sister Yao char koay kak, Kafe Ping Hooi CKT, Pitt St koay teow th'ng, apom carts.

sources.title: https://thebackpackingfamily.com/what-are-the-best-penang-hawkers/
sources.claim: Hawker-centre orientation: New World Park is the convenient George Town option; New Lane is the more authentic locals' street.

sources.title: https://www.nationalgeographic.com/travel/article/best-places-to-eat-in-george-town-malaysia-food-guide
sources.claim: George Town is described by a local as a premier place to eat in Malaysia / Asia.

sources.title: https://guide.michelin.com/en/article/michelin-guide-ceremony/malaysia-bib-gourmand-2026
sources.claim: 2026 Bib Gourmand: 58 eateries across KL & Penang; three new Penang additions (Awesome Char Koay Teow, Bee Hwa Cafe, Sifu); Ah Leng among Penang Bibs.

sources.title: https://guide.michelin.com/en/article/michelin-guide-ceremony/malaysia-full-selection-2026
sources.claim: New MICHELIN Selected Penang entries 2026: Blacklinen, Du-An, Memoire, Peninsula House, Sood by Chef Ton.

sources.title: https://www.buletinmutiara.com/penang-continues-to-impress-in-michelin-guide-2026/
sources.claim: Penang in Michelin 2026: 74 listings, 33 Bib Gourmand; two one-stars (Au Jardin, Auntie Gaik Lean's) retained; new Selected entries.

sources.title: https://www.malaymail.com/news/eat-drink/2025/11/11/michelin-guide-kuala-lumpur-and-penang-2026-bib-gourmand-list-has-five-new-entrants-three-dropped/198038
sources.claim: 2026 Bib Gourmand list had five new entrants and three dropped across KL & Penang.

sources.title: https://guide.michelin.com/my/en/pulau-pinang/my-george-town/restaurant/siam-road-char-koay-teow
sources.claim: Siam Road Char Koay Teow is a 2026 Michelin Bib Gourmand charcoal-wok CKT stall in George Town.

sources.title: https://guide.michelin.com/my/en/pulau-pinang/my-george-town/restaurant/penang-road-famous-jin-kor-char-kuey-teow
sources.claim: Penang Road Famous Jin Kor Char Kuey Teow (in the Joo Hooi food court) is a Michelin Bib Gourmand CKT.

sources.title: https://eatbook.sg/best-penang-char-kway-teow/
sources.claim: Siam Road CKT is most famous with hour-long weekend waits (RM8-11); Lorong Selamat RM12-15 with red-beret aunty.

sources.title: https://smartdory.com/2026/04/air-itam-laksa-penang/
sources.claim: Air Itam Laksa at foot of Kek Lok Si: legendary corner stall (served Bourdain 2012), weekends-only; nearby 2828 daily ~RM7-8.

sources.title: https://www.springtomorrow.com/air-itam-laksa-penang/
sources.claim: Air Itam assam laksa is rated among the best in Penang; sharp, spicy, poached-mackerel broth.

sources.title: https://penanglicious.com/best-nasi-kandar-in-penang/
sources.claim: Top Penang nasi kandar includes Deens Maju, Line Clear, and Hameediyah (est. 1907, oldest in Malaysia, 10am-10pm).

sources.title: https://penangfoodie.com/top-10-best-nasi-kandar-in-penang/
sources.claim: Deens Maju on Jalan Gurdwara known for crispy fried chicken and rich gravy; open daily but closed Fridays.

sources.title: https://www.tripadvisor.com/Restaurant_Review-g298303-d3858927-Reviews-Nasi_Kandar_Line_Clear-George_Town_Penang_Island_Penang.html
sources.claim: Line Clear nasi kandar is an alley institution beside 161/177 Penang Road, open 24 hours.

sources.title: https://smartdory.com/2026/02/penang-hokkien-mee-new-world-park/
sources.claim: A New World Park stall serves Penang Hokkien (prawn) mee perfected over 50 years with rich prawn-sweet broth.

sources.title: https://guide.michelin.com/us/en/pulau-pinang/my-george-town/restaurant/888-hokkien-mee-lebuh-presgrave
sources.claim: 888 Hokkien Mee on Lebuh Presgrave is a Michelin-listed prawn-noodle stall with prawn-head red broth, 30+ years.

sources.title: https://chendul.my/
sources.claim: Penang Road Famous Teochew Chendul official site; business started selling chendul at Penang Road in 1936.

sources.title: https://www.tripadvisor.com.au/Restaurant_Review-g660694-d4801157-Reviews-Penang_Road_Famous_Teochew_Cendol-Penang_Island_Penang.html
sources.claim: The Lebuh Keng Kwee cendol stall is a hugely popular spot with long queues.

sources.title: https://eatbook.sg/chulia-street-night-market/
sources.claim: Chulia Street night hawker (6pm-12am): Mother & Son Wantan Mee (~50 yrs), lok lok, ham chee peng, viral 80-sen apom aunty; bring cash.

sources.title: https://thesmartlocal.my/chulia-street-night-hawker/
sources.claim: Chulia Street night hawker has iconic decades-old food stalls in George Town's core.

sources.title: https://www.tripadvisor.com/Restaurant_Review-g298303-d3706666-Reviews-Toh_Soon_Cafe-George_Town_Penang_Island_Penang.html
sources.claim: Toh Soon Café (Lebuh Campbell) is a quintessential old Penang kopitiam with homemade kaya, charcoal toast, robusta coffee, 8am-5pm.

sources.title: https://www.yelp.com/biz/kheng-pin-cafe-george-town-3
sources.claim: Kheng Pin Café (80 Jln Penang) is a traditional kopitiam housing famous loh bak, char koay teow, prawn mee, wonton mee stalls.

sources.title: https://www.viator.com/Penang-tours/Cooking-Classes/d339-g6-c19
sources.claim: Penang cooking classes incl. Penang Chiak (market tour + breakfast + cooking from Chow Rasta Market, ~8:10am start); small-group food tours.

sources.title: https://www.nazlinaspicestation.com/
sources.claim: Nazlina Spice Station runs Malaysia's longest-running cooking classes/market tours (since 2009), Lonely Planet listed, sessions Sat/Sun/Tue/Thu.

sources.title: https://www.tripadvisor.co.uk/Attraction_Review-g298303-d2414160-Reviews-Penang_Homecooking_School-George_Town_Penang_Island_Penang.html
sources.claim: Penang Homecooking School: choose dishes (CKT, roti canai) by email, RM350 pp, with breakfast and market tour.

sources.title: https://penangfoodie.com/best-penang-curry-mee/
sources.claim: Lorong Seratus Tahun curry mee (~50 yrs) ideal as breakfast; Nyonya-style curry mee available at Air Itam morning market.

sources.title: https://www.tripadvisor.com/Restaurant_Review-g298303-d886731-Reviews-Lorong_Seratus_Tahun_Curry_Mee-George_Town_Penang_Island_Penang.html
sources.claim: Lorong Seratus Tahun is widely called the best curry mee in Penang, with cockles, pig's blood, tofu puff, prawns and dark chilli sauce.

sources.title: https://www.lexissuitespenang.com/media/blogs/must-try-famous-food-in-balik-pulau
sources.claim: Balik Pulau food: Kim Laksa serving since the 1940s; choice of Penang asam laksa or creamy Thai laksa; durian.

sources.title: https://www.penang-insider.com/balik-pulau-travel-guide/
sources.claim: Balik Pulau rural west: nutmeg infuses local dishes (asam laksa, ais kacang); Bao Sheng durian farm hilltop retreat.

sources.title: https://kebaya.com.my/
sources.claim: Kebaya Dining Room at Seven Terraces serves refined Peranakan/Indochinese set menus in a restored heritage terrace.

sources.title: https://www.georgetownheritage.com/best-nyonya-restaurants-penang/
sources.claim: Kebaya serves among the best Peranakan/Nyonya fare in Penang, in the restored Seven Terraces; multi-course set menu format.

sources.title: https://guide.michelin.com/en/pulau-pinang/my-george-town/restaurant/auntie-gaik-lean-s-old-school-eatery
sources.claim: Auntie Gaik Lean's Old School Eatery is a one-Michelin-Star authentic Nyonya restaurant in George Town (hand-cut nasi ulam, up to 10 ulam).

sources.title: https://danielfooddiary.com/2025/05/03/auntiegaiklean/
sources.claim: Auntie Gaik Lean's is Michelin-starred Peranakan with reservations a must.

sources.title: https://penanghillco.com.my/
sources.claim: David Brown's Hill Top Garden Restaurant is on Penang Hill (official).

sources.title: https://www.tripadvisor.com/Restaurant_Review-g660694-d2061893-Reviews-David_Brown_s_Restaurant_and_Tea_Terraces-Penang_Island_Penang.html
sources.claim: David Brown's is the highest restaurant on Penang Hill, a garden tea-terrace with George Town views, daily 11am-10pm.

sources.title: https://penangtime.com/review/gurney-drive-hawker-centre/
sources.claim: Gurney Drive Hawker Centre is a seafront ~100-stall hub; best ~7-8pm at sunset; packed on weekends, arrive early/late.

sources.title: https://malaysiafact.com/penang-jetty-chew-guide-travel-tips-2026/
sources.claim: Chew Jetty stilt village has a food court at the entrance and walkway stalls (laksa, CKT, cendol, grilled seafood, durian ice-cream).

sources.title: https://onpenang.com/clan-jetties-of-penang/
sources.claim: Clan jetties are floating heritage villages; stalls operate daytime, more options earlier in the day.

sources.title: https://my.trip.com/guide/info/best-time-to-visit-penang.html
sources.claim: Best time to visit Penang is the dry season Dec-Feb (mid-Nov to mid-Feb), avoiding the hotter Apr-Aug.

sources.title: https://onpenang.com/best-time-to-visit/
sources.claim: Penang's wetter monsoon season runs roughly May-October, with heavier rain usually in short bursts.

sources.title: https://durianpenang.com/calendar
sources.claim: Penang's main durian season peaks mid-year (June-August) with best volume, variety and prices.

sources.title: https://wise.com/gb/currency-converter/eur-to-myr-rate
sources.claim: Mid-2026 EUR to MYR mid-market rate is approximately 1 EUR = RM 4.7.

sources.title: https://georgetowncity.my/banana-leaf-rice-in-penang-that-you-have-to-try/
sources.claim: Veloo Villas in Little India (30+ yrs) is known for banana-leaf rice; Hameediyah a Little India landmark.

sources.title: https://www.showmemalaysia.com/best-dim-sum-spots-penang/
sources.claim: Tai Tong is a historic Chinatown teahouse with trolley dim sum from breakfast; queues ~7:30am; ~RM30 pp.

sources.title: https://foreverbreak.com/travel/malaysia/penang/batu-ferringhi-night-market/
sources.claim: Batu Ferringhi night market (beach belt) runs 7-11pm nightly with satay, seafood and mixed/international fare; cash/e-wallet.

sources.title: https://en.tripadvisor.com.hk/Restaurant_Review-g635527-d1772228-Reviews-or2565-Long_Beach-Batu_Ferringhi_Penang_Island_Penang.html
sources.claim: Long Beach Café at Batu Ferringhi is a beachside food court mixing Malaysian and international dishes.

sources.title: https://www.springtomorrow.com/new-lane-hawker-centre-penang/
sources.claim: New Lane / Lorong Baru is a vehicle-free evening locals' hawker street (CKT, oh chien, loh bak, satay), 4-10/11pm, closed Wed.

sources.title: https://jumppy.com.sg/penang-hawker-centre-guide/
sources.claim: 2026 hawker guide: single dish runs RM5-15 (most plates RM6-10); covers Gurney, New Lane, Lorong Baru, Pulau Tikus.

sources.title: https://www.lokalocal.com/blog/food/penang-private-home-dining/
sources.claim: Penang supper clubs / private dining incl. Pennapra, Third Culture (Pulau Tikus), Auction Rooms (Kimberley Hotel).

sources.title: https://www.instagram.com/pennapraprivatedining/
sources.claim: Pennapra Private Dining + Supperclub offers reservation-only modern Thai tasting menus, no walk-ins.

sources.title: https://thesmartlocal.my/bakeries-in-penang/
sources.claim: ChinaHouse (Beach St) spans three heritage shophouses with ~30 cakes daily, 9am-1am; Mugshot Café (Chulia St) famed for bagels.

sources.title: https://guide.michelin.com/my/en/article/dining-out/behind-the-bib-penang-road-famous-laksa
sources.claim: Penang Road Famous Laksa is a storied Bib Gourmand assam-laksa institution profiled by Michelin.

sources.title: https://www.tripadvisor.com/Attraction_Review-g660694-d5990546-Reviews-or10-Pulau_Tikus_Markets-Penang_Island_Penang.html
sources.claim: Pulau Tikus Market offers a 6:30-11am breakfast hawker section (dim sum, curry mee, prawn mee, kuih) and a popular night food-court.
